lesson.subtitle: Lesson 7 -- The Best Team, The Biggest Challenge
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Viviane Rodrigues de Oliveira | Lesson 7 -- The Best Team, The Biggest Challenge

listenings.text: For years I presented the worst slides in the company. Twenty numbers, four colours, and a board that stopped listening after the first minute. The change came from our finance director, who told me something I did not want to hear. He said: your data is the best in this company and your slide is the hardest to read. So I tried something different. One slide, three sentences. The strongest number of the quarter. The biggest problem. And the root cause of that problem, in one line. The first time I did it the meeting was silent for about ten seconds, and then the CEO asked the best question he has ever asked me: what do you need from us? Twenty numbers had never produced that question. Three sentences did.

What is your biggest weakness. I know, it is the worst question in the interview, and I still ask it, because the answer tells me more than the CV. The most common answer is the fake one: I am a perfectionist, I work too hard, I care too much. When I hear that, I write nothing down. The best answers have two parts. The real weakness, said simply. And what you are doing about it. For example: my English is not strong yet, and I have a class every week and I am recording myself. That is a better answer than any perfect CV, because it tells me you can look at yourself honestly and then act. And a small thing that is not small. If your weakness is a language, never say I do not speak English. Say I am learning, and here is where I am. One is a door closing. The other is a door opening.

extra_audio.text: Engagement is seventy-four per cent, the highest we have ever had. Our biggest challenge is store retention. The north region has the lowest engagement in the company. The root cause is the first month, not the salary.
